Transfer learning on the pre-train model¶

Project flow

  • Data loading and preprocessing
  • Model preperation
  • Fine Tuening and training
  • Model evaluation
  • Comparision of the result
  • Prediction using the best fit model

About the data set and pre training models¶

Dataset
I am using the cifar100 data set which is a set of images of 32X32(3 channel) to train my model to identify the images.
The images has 100 labels i.e. there are image of 100 different type of object, animals, people etc.
The data set is of 50000 training image and 10000 testing images.

Models
I am testing the cifar 100 dataset on three pre train models. These are

  • Restnet (Resiudal Network)
  • VGG16
  • Mobilenet V2 - This is a lighter version of the image processing model

All of these three models are pretrain on imagenet dataset

Loading the libraires and Data¶

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.datasets import cifar100
from tensorflow.keras.applications.resnet50 import preprocess_input as preprocess_resnet50
from tensorflow.keras.applications.vgg16 import preprocess_input as preprocess_vgg16
from tensorflow.keras.applications.mobilenet_v2 import preprocess_input as preprocess_mobilenetv2
(X_train, y_train),(X_test,y_test) = cifar100.load_data()

Preprocessing the data set according to the features of the model imput images¶

X_train_resnet50 = preprocess_resnet50(X_train)
X_train_vgg16 = preprocess_vgg16(X_train)
X_train_mobilenetv2 = preprocess_mobilenetv2(X_train)
X_test_resnet50 = preprocess_resnet50(X_test)
X_test_vgg16 = preprocess_vgg16(X_test)
X_test_mobilenetv2 = preprocess_mobilenetv2(X_test)

Model preperation¶

Load and modify pre-trained models to fit the CIFAR-100 classification task.

Using ResNet50¶
base_model_resnet50 = ResNet50(weights='imagenet', include_top=False, input_shape=(32, 32, 3))
model_resnet50 = Model(inputs = base_model_resnet50.input, outputs = predictions)
model_resnet50.compile(optimizer='adam', loss = 'sparse_categorical_crossentropy', metrics = ['accuracy'])

Fine tuning (Training the model on cifar dataset)¶

This is also called as transfer learning since the model already has the weight of the imagenet dataset. I am adjusting weight of the last few layers of the network based on my own dataset I will train the model for 30 epoch using the early_stopping methods to avoid any unnecessary epoch which may not improve the model

Prediction¶

  • Using Resnet to do the prediction since it has outperformed the other model in validation accurancy.
  • Identify the correct and incorrectly predicted label
  • Randomly select 100 correct and 100 incorrectly predicted image
  • Display them into 20 X20 grid highlighting the incorrect labels
313/313 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 190s 593ms/step

Conclusion¶

  • Among the three models the ResNet50 has outperformed in terms of validation accuracy and loss.
  • ResNet50 shows 40% accuracy after running for 5 epoch. Which mean the model is 400 times better than any random guess where probability of selection a correct picture is 1 out of 1000 images
  • The patient level is set at 3, which means that the model will stop if there is any three epoch with not improvement in validation loss. Setting the patient level to default and training the model for higher epoch will improve the accuracy of the model.
  • Running high epoch is computationally expensive for this data set due to 3 channel images.
  • Batch processing the training data may reduce the training time

Limitation and suggestion¶

  • The there are only 600 images per level are available for training the data.
  • The hardware limitation and computationally expensive in running the model for large epochs
  • Experiment with different hyperparameters (learning rate, number of epochs, batch size).
  • Implement data augmentation techniques may help in creating new data for the model training
  • Fine-tuning different numbers of layers.
